posts.title: An autumn concert in the garden
posts.excerpt: A string trio played under the maple, and the tea ran out twice.
posts.content:
On Saturday afternoon a string trio from the local music school played in the garden for an hour. Residents brought blankets, families brought grandchildren, and the kitchen baked two hundred small apple cakes.

The next concert is planned for the spring. If you know a group that would like to play for our residents, please talk to the front desk.

posts.title: Five ways we help residents eat well
posts.excerpt: Shared tables, soft versions of the same dish and a cup of tea in the afternoon.
posts.content:
Many people come to us after months of eating little at home. The first change is simple: meals at a shared table, with the same faces every day. Appetite often returns within weeks.

Our kitchen makes soft and minced versions of each dish rather than a separate menu, adds an afternoon tea, and weighs residents once a month so the dietitian can adjust portions early.

posts.title: Two standard rooms available from November
posts.excerpt: Both rooms face the garden; tours run every day.
posts.content:
Two standard rooms on the first floor become available in November. Both face south over the garden and have their own washroom.

Tours run every day at 10:00 and 14:00. Call the front desk to book a time, and bring the person who may move in if you can.
